The bridge is falling apart. Everyone knows it. Engineers rated it structurally deficient in 2019. The city council debated repairs for three years. They studied the problem. They commissioned reports. They held public forums. They did everything except fix the bridge. Meanwhile, forty thousand cars cross it every day. Trucks loaded with freight. School buses carrying children. The estimated repair cost was twelve million dollars. The estimated replacement cost is now eighty million. That is what delay buys you -- a bigger bill and a greater risk. Last month a chunk of concrete fell from the underside and landed on a pickup truck. The driver was not hurt. Next time the outcome could be different. Infrastructure is not glamorous. It does not win elections. It does not generate headlines -- until it fails. Then it generates funerals. The time to act was years ago. The next best time is now.
